Question: What was the most disturbing thing you saw as an adult?
Answer: The story of Hisashi Ouchi, who Suffered An Excruciating and most painful death in the history On September 30, 1999, technicians at Tokaimura nuclear plant in Japan accidentally caused a horrific chain reaction that changed the lives of everyone around them, including themselves. The man closest to the accident, Hisashi Ouchi, would suffer the worst consequences of all, becoming the most radioactive man in history. Hisachi Ouchi, started working in the plant as a technician in the late 1980s. The purpose of the plant was to convert uranium hexafluoride into enriched uranium for use in nuclear energy, This process needed to be very precise and each step should be conducted carefully and timed perfectly, each element mixed in exact proportions. Since Workers had already missed a deadline for productions, their bosses imposed for generating this fuel, by cutting the essential steps of safety procedures to increase the production speed. So on the morning of September 30, Hisachi Ouchi, along with his co-worker Masato Shinohara, and his 54-year-old supervisor Yutaka Yokokawa, decided to try one more shortcut. The problem is, despite the fact that they all had years of experience on the job - Ouchi had been working at the plant for more than ten years at that point but none of them had been trained well enough to know what they were doing, or what the horrific effects of doing the wrong thing could be. This negligence caused a lethal explosion due to which Ouchi, who was standing directly over the steel bucket when the reaction happened…had absorbed 17 Sieverts of radiation, where the “safe” level of radiation for humans to absorb within a year is just 100 milliSieverts. Ouchi experienced one of the most brutally painful and slow deaths in history. He had severe radiation burns on his whole body, and his eyes were leaking blood. His white blood cells were almost fully wiped out, and he had experienced severe, horrific damage to all his major organs Three days later he was transferred to the University of Tokyo Hospital. In his first week at the hospital, doctors tried experimental cancer treatments to replenish his white blood cells. They also performed almost constant skin grafts and blood transfusions. The process was unbelievably torturous for Ouchi. After just a week at the hospital, he begged the doctors to let him go. “I can’t take it anymore….I am not a guinea pig.” Unfortunately, the doctors, partly thanks to Ouchi’s own family’s wishes…. they refused to sign DNR - (do not resuscitate) - paperwork. His body that it killed off all the new cells it came into contact with. The radiation thwarted doctors’ every attempt to keep Ouchi alive. It had damaged his chromosomes beyond repair. Soon, Ouchi’s skin would start to melt and detach from his body. The extent of his suffering at this point was extreme. After 59 days in the hospital, Ouchi suffered a heart attack. However, his family had given instructions to resuscitate him should the worst happen, so the doctors did. At one point, Ouchi had three heart attacks in one hour. He suffered even more and more brain damage. For the last few weeks of his hospital stay, he was barely responsive. The body of Hisashi Ouchi , after his skin fell of due to radiation Finally, after 83 days, one final heart attack sent Ouchi over the edge he’d been dangling off for weeks. On December 21, 1999, after multi-organ-system failure, Ouchi’s heart gave out and he died.
